title: Cempaka Seri: rethinking the townhouse.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #150 | CEMPAKA SERI, KOTA SERIEMAS
excerpt: Thoughtful interiors and room for greenery put a familiar housing format in a different light.
takeaways: A strata townhouse built into sloping ground, with green buffers between rows.
An upper unit of about 1,800 sq ft with a double-height living room, priced around RM380,000.
A quiet own-stay location that suits people working around KLIA and Nilai.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Cempaka Seri is a strata townhouse in Kota Seriemas built into sloping ground, so the rows step with the terrain and green strips separate them. It avoids the usual townhouse complaints of a narrow entrance, awkward structure and dark corners.

The upper unit Sean visits has about 1,800 sq ft: a ground-level store room for heavy things, a 4-ft-wide staircase, a double-height living room about six metres high and two windows in almost every room. It was selling for around RM380,000.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: Kota Seriemas is a 2,400-acre township started in 2000, beside Nilai and close to KLIA and Putrajaya, linked by LEKAS and the North-South Expressway. Inside are tree-lined roads, cycle paths, a lake park, a golf club and a university college; the back way in, past Kampung Salak Tinggi, is far more rural.

pros: Space and build quality: no narrow entrance, no awkward structure and no dark corners, with the store room downstairs, the double-height living room and slit windows in the bedrooms as highlights.
Open space in balance with buildings: green areas between rows and an organic layout that works with the changes in level.
The price: about RM380,000 for some 1,800 sq ft near Nilai, KLIA and several colleges, with lower units renting for about RM1,500 according to the developer's team.
cons: The pandemic hit its core buyers, many of whom work in aviation.
Arriving through the rural roads around Kampung Salak Tinggi makes it feel undeveloped; the highway approach doesn't.
It is purely an own-stay location: very quiet, with little commercial activity, so it suits families working nearby, not people commuting to KL.

closing: A well-designed, affordable family home if you work around KLIA or Nilai; hard to justify for a daily commute to KL.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this March 2021 episode. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three concerns he names, in his order, at the end of the video. The developer's team showed Sean around.
